correlates.name: Digoxin (Digitalis) and Contractility
correlates.presentation: increased Ca²⁺ available for contraction → positive inotropy (increased cardiac contractility).
correlates.pathophysiology: Digoxin inhibits the Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase, raising intracellular Na⁺. The elevated intracellular Na⁺ drives the Na⁺/Ca²⁺ exchanger into reverse mode (pumps Na⁺ out, brings Ca²⁺ in), increasing intracellular Ca²⁺.

correlates.name: Hyperkalemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Elevated extracellular K⁺ raises (makes less negative) the resting membrane potential, shortening the distance to threshold — but sustained depolarization impairs Na⁺ channel recovery (recovery needs Vm below threshold).
correlates.treatment: Because severe hyperkalemia arrests the heart, cardioplegia solution (high K⁺) is used intentionally to stop the heart during open-heart surgery and transplantation.

correlates.name: Hypokalemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Low extracellular K⁺ makes Vm more negative (would lower excitability), but the dominant effect is decreased K⁺ conductance — fewer K⁺ channels open, slowing repolarization and prolonging AP duration.

transporters.name: Fast Na+ Channel (I_Na)
transporters.location: Atrial, ventricular and His-Purkinje myocytes — everywhere except the SA and AV nodes
transporters.function: Carries phase 0 of the fast-response action potential, driving an upstroke faster than 100 V/s once threshold near -55 mV is reached
transporters.regulation: Has two gates, and its recovery from inactivation is what sets the effective refractory period in fast fibers
transporters.inhibitor: Class I antiarrhythmics; also blocked by tricyclic antidepressants, which is why they widen the QRS

transporters.name: I_K1 (Inward Rectifier K+ Channel)
transporters.function: Holds the resting membrane potential near -90 mV during phase 4 and contributes to phase 3 repolarization
transporters.regulation: Its progressive closure during late phase 4 contributes to pacemaker depolarization in nodal tissue
transporters.inhibitor: Not a therapeutic target; hyperkalemia alters its behavior and produces the peaked T wave

transporters.name: I_to (Transient Outward K+ Current)
transporters.function: Produces phase 1, the brief notch of early repolarization immediately after the sodium upstroke
transporters.regulation: Density varies across the ventricular wall, which is part of why epicardium and endocardium repolarize differently

transporters.name: Delayed Rectifier K+ Channel
transporters.function: Opposes calcium entry during the phase 2 plateau and then dominates phase 3 repolarization, setting action potential duration
transporters.regulation: Balanced against L-type calcium current during the plateau
transporters.inhibitor: Class III antiarrhythmics, which prolong action potential duration and therefore the effective refractory period

transporters.name: T-type Calcium Channel
transporters.function: Contributes to late phase 4 depolarization, helping carry the pacemaker potential up to threshold
transporters.regulation: Transient and low-threshold, opening at more negative potentials than the L-type channel
transporters.inhibitor: Not selectively targeted by the standard calcium channel blockers

transporters.name: Na+/Ca2+ Exchanger (NCX)
transporters.function: Extrudes 1 Ca2+ in exchange for 3 Na+ entering, so the net charge movement is depolarizing; it is a main route of calcium removal during relaxation
transporters.regulation: Runs in reverse when intracellular sodium is high — the mechanism behind digoxin's inotropy and its toxicity
transporters.inhibitor: Indirectly by digoxin, which raises intracellular sodium by blocking the Na+/K+ ATPase

transporters.name: SERCA
transporters.location: Sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane of cardiac myocytes
transporters.function: An ATP-driven pump that reloads the SR with calcium, ending contraction and setting up the next beat
transporters.regulation: Released from phospholamban inhibition when PKA phosphorylates it during beta-1 stimulation, which speeds relaxation (lusitropy)

transporters.name: Ryanodine Receptor
transporters.location: Sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane of cardiac myocytes
transporters.function: The calcium release channel of calcium-induced calcium release — a small L-type calcium entry triggers a large SR calcium release that actually drives contraction
transporters.regulation: Opened by calcium entering through L-type channels during phase 2
transporters.inhibitor: Ryanodine experimentally; dantrolene acts on the skeletal muscle isoform

formulas.name: Cardiac Equilibrium Potentials
formulas.equation: E_K about -96 mV, E_Na about +52 mV, E_Ca about +134 mV
formulas.meaning: Each phase of the action potential drives membrane voltage toward the equilibrium potential of whichever ion is conducting, which is why phase 0 shoots positive and phase 3 returns negative
formulas.normalValue: Resting membrane potential about -90 mV, set by I_K1

formulas.name: Fast vs Slow Response Action Potentials
formulas.equation: Fast response phase 0 = Na+ current; slow response phase 0 = L-type Ca2+ current
formulas.meaning: Only the SA and AV nodes use the slow response, which is precisely why calcium channel blockers act on nodal tissue while sodium channel blockers act on working myocardium and Purkinje fibers
formulas.normalValue: Upstroke velocity over 100 V/s for fast fibers versus about 10 V/s for slow
